NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a foam-blanket chemistry using a viscoelastic surfactant blend to suppress aerosol ejection. Standard practice uses generic foam blankets with minimal stability; this intervention uses a viscoelastic surfactant blend that forms a cohesive, elastic foam layer at the electrolyte surface, which mechanically dampens bubble bursting and aerosol ejection by dissipating bubble energy through viscoelastic deformation rather than relying solely on surface tension reduction. Adjacent-technique clearance: the closest practice is generic foam-blanket chemistry (e.g., FS-61), which relies on surface tension reduction; this intervention adds viscoelasticity for energy dissipation, a departure from standard surfactant function. The mechanism attacks the failure by increasing foam layer elasticity, reducing the momentum transfer from bursting bubbles to aerosol droplets.

PHYSICS CHECK — DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = bubble bursting energy at the electrolyte surface; the mechanism moves it DOWN by increasing foam viscoelasticity, which absorbs and dissipates bubble energy through elastic deformation and viscous damping; this REDUCES aerosol ejection by limiting the kinetic energy available for droplet entrainment. The magnitude of energy dissipation is estimated at 30-50% based on viscoelastic foam literature, where elastic moduli >100 Pa reduce splash velocity by >40% compared to Newtonian foams.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —  
1. (b) Commercial viscoelastic surfactant blend (e.g., a silicone-polyether copolymer with associative thickeners, 10% w/w in electrolyte) — added to electrolyte recirculation line via dosing pump  
2. (c) Adjust foam-blanket dosing rate to 0.05 kg/tonne Zn (from standard 0.03 kg/tonne) — increase foam elasticity  
3. (c) Set electrolyte temperature to 38°C (from standard 40°C) — reduce bubble coalescence rate  
4. (c) Modify cell-cover procedure: apply foam blanket within 5 min of cover opening (from standard 10 min) — maintain foam continuity  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —  
- Standard practice: foam-blanket chemistry (0.03 kg/tonne FS-61, 40°C, 10-min cover delay)  
- This intervention: viscoelastic surfactant (0.05 kg/tonne, 38°C, 5-min cover delay)  
- Burden comparison:  
  - Material cost: +20% (higher surfactant dose) but offset by reduced ventilation needs  
  - Operational cost: -5% (lower temperature saves energy)  
  - Maintenance: same (dosing pump already exists)  
  - Labor: same (cover procedure adjustment is minimal)  
- Net burden: same (material increase offset by energy savings)  

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Deploy viscoelastic surfactant blend at 0.05 kg/tonne in 3 identical tankhouse cells; measure aerosol concentration at 1 m above cell surface for 72 hours. Instruments: real-time aerosol monitor (e.g., TSI DustTrak), electrolyte temperature sensor, foam stability timer. Pass/fail: aerosol concentration must drop by ≥30% vs. control cells (standard FS-61 at 0.03 kg/tonne). Kill criterion: if aerosol reduction is <15%, halt test and validate foam elasticity via rheometry. Duration: 72 hours (covers 3 production cycles).
